pairs.difference: A: the neck pillow is tilted and fills most of the card, leaving about 11% at the edges, like the tilted ticket and glove on the real cards. B: the sheriff star is small (0.193, at the bottom of the real range), seen straight on, symmetric and dead-center in the concentric rings, with even empty purple on every side.
pairs.fix: Draw the sheriff star larger, tilted about 20 degrees and turned slightly in 3/4 view, filling most of the card and sitting a little off-center.

pairs.difference: A: the harmonica lies on a diagonal from lower left to upper right. It is wide but short (height 0.473, below the real range), which is normal for a long thin object. B: the fan is open, tilted and fills the upper-middle of the card with a good margin. Both read at once at thumbnail size and nothing competes with either.

A: the scout jacket is nearly front-on and centered. At thumbnail size the row of four badges on the green sash pulls the eye away from the jacket's outline. B: the cowboy hat is in 3/4 view, tilted, fills the width, and reads as one clean outline.
pairs.fix: Turn the jacket to a 3/4 angle, tilt it slightly and make it larger. Use fewer, larger badges so the jacket's outline reads first.

pairs.difference: A: the caravan is in 3/4 view, large and low in the card, and the grass runs off the bottom edge, like the real lawnmower card. B: the buoy is narrow (width 0.535, below the real range), perfectly centered and symmetric, seen front-on, with water and clouds filling the space on both sides. This matches the centered, front-on lighthouse in the generated lesson cards.
pairs.fix: Show the buoy from a 3/4 angle, larger and slightly off-center. Let the water run off the bottom edge and leave less empty sky on the sides.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers sit low, in the bottom half. The orange wall and cream floor split the card with a hard horizontal line, leaving a big empty top half, and the subject is short (0.487) with a 0.033 edge margin. B: the boots stand upright, fill the middle of the card and sit on a smooth green gradient.
pairs.fix: Draw the sneakers bigger and higher in the card, angled toward the viewer. Use a soft gradient background with no hard horizon line.

pairs.difference: A: the cactus is front-on, symmetric and dead-center, a narrow column (width 0.567, below the real range) with sunburst space on both sides and pebbles around the base. B: the spring duck is in profile, off-center and slightly wider. Both sit on a sand patch with stones.
pairs.fix: Turn the cactus to a slight 3/4 angle and move it off-center. Make it wider, with its arms reaching toward the card edges, and drop the scattered pebbles.

pairs.difference: A: the bandana is tilted, off-center to the upper left, and its knot reaches toward the right edge, like the real tilted cards. B: the graduation cap is level and centered on concentric rings and is short (height 0.506), with a lot of empty ring space above and below.
pairs.fix: Tilt the graduation cap about 15 degrees, show it in 3/4 view and make it larger so it fills more of the card's height.

pairs.difference: A: the boxing gloves sit low on a table, are cut off at the left edge (width 0.951, margin 0.021, both outside the real range) and leave a large empty blue wall above. B: the saddle is centered on the fence with clear margins, and the fence rails run off both sides as context.
pairs.fix: Draw the boxing gloves fully inside the card, larger and centered higher, with a small margin on every side and less empty wall above.

pairs.difference: A: the rocking chair is in 3/4 view, fills the card and rises nearly to the top. B: the covered wagon is short (height 0.556) and sits in the upper middle. A wide strip of empty dirt fills the bottom third and the drawbar pulls the eye toward the lower right.
pairs.fix: Draw the wagon larger and lower in the card, filling more of its height, with less empty ground in front.

pairs.difference: B is the same lighthouse as the real lesson card: tight framing, cut off by the bottom edge. A: the windmill is shown whole, grounded in a grass field. Its wheel sits upper-left and the tail vane leaves a lot of empty sky, so the weight is lopsided. The generated lessons share this whole-object-on-ground staging.
pairs.fix: Frame the windmill closer so the tower is cut off by the bottom edge, and make the wheel larger and nearer the center.

pairs.difference: A: a full scene. The campfire competes with a large teapot on a stone, a log cabin cut off at the top left, pine trees and grass tufts, so the first read is split. B: the coin binoculars are one clear hero, cut off at the bottom like the real lighthouse, with a soft city behind them.
pairs.fix: Show only the campfire, larger and centered. Remove the teapot and cabin, and use a simple soft background.

pairs.difference: A: the phone booth is in 3/4 view, tall and narrow (width 0.512), against a patterned wall. B: the trophy is perfectly symmetric, front-on and dead-center on a blue pedestal under a spotlight. This is the centered, on-a-base staging seen in the generated lesson cards.
pairs.fix: Show the trophy at a 3/4 angle with a slight tilt, larger and off-center, and remove the pedestal and spotlight.

pattern: On composition, generated cards place the whole object front-on or symmetric, dead-center, with even empty space on every side. They often stand it on a base, plinth or patch of ground and add extra props. Real cards tilt the hero or use a 3/4 view, push it close to an edge or let an edge cut it off, and keep a single hero with nothing competing.
